content.title: About
content.content: Bouillabaisse is a traditional Provençal fish stew made with several types of seafood, fish, shellfish, tomatoes, saffron and aromatic herbs. Served hot, often accompanied by croutons and rouille.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bouillabaisse originated in the port of Marseille, where fishermen used unsold catch to make a flavorful broth.
The classic recipe calls for at least three fish species: sea bass, rascasse, and conger eel.
Saffron, which gives the dish its golden hue, was historically an expensive spice, so it was used sparingly.
Marseille hosts an annual "Bouillabaisse Competition" where judges evaluate aroma, taste and presentation.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish and shellfish provide EPA and DHA, supporting heart and brain health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The stew supplies a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cod, sea bass and shellfish are abundant in B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iodine, zinc, selenium
items.content: Seafood is a good source of trace elements that boost immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomatoes and saffron
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes and crocin in saffron help combat free radicals.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish or shellfish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bouillabaisse often contains added salt and fish sauce, so people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly cooked shellfish can harbor toxins; always use fresh ingredients and cook thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot in a deep bowl, often with toasted croutons topped with rouille (garlic‑saffron mayo) and a sprinkle of fresh parsley. A squeeze of lemon brightens the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat to a rolling boil to ensure safety.
